checks.name: sheila
checks.about: Sheila, the Pi Coding Agent, takes Bridge tasks through this machine's machine-lane worker. The check's own line names each blocker. 'worker: ... not active' means the user unit agent-bridge-worker-machine.service is stopped or crashed: journalctl --user -u agent-bridge-worker-machine -n 80, then systemctl --user restart agent-bridge-worker-machine (safe; it also carries bati-desktop, and a task it held is re-leased by the gateway). 'pi: does not start' means node/pi under ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.18.0 is broken. 'login: stale' is EG's to fix (run pi on BATI and /login); do not copy or edit ~/.pi/agent/auth.json, and do not touch ~/.pi-bridge. 'jail: bubblewrap missing' needs sudo -n apt-get install -y bubblewrap. Never widen her card, her jail or the gateway's scopes to make this pass.

checks.name: todos
checks.about: A todo that may be worked has waited more than 30 minutes in inbox/new, or one has sat in inbox/in_process past the agent timeout plus 30 minutes. The watch already starts the todo worker every run, so look at why it does not take it: background.log (the latest 'todo --work' run), the locks folder, the interpreter named here. Run adw_machine_todo.py --work once to see. Never delete, move or resend a todo.

checks.name: adw-log
checks.about: The latest run of a supervisor ADW (todo --work, mail --flush, supervise, receive) in background.log ended in a Python traceback. Read the traceback under that adw id, fix the cause (a missing module, a bad path, a broken interpreter), then run that same ADW once so its latest run ends cleanly. Do not edit or truncate the log.

checks.name: disk
checks.about: Less than 10 GB free on the home directory's filesystem. Find what grew (du -xh --max-depth=2 ~ | sort -h | tail). Removing anything but caches you can name is EG's decision: put it in needs.

checks.name: held-mail
checks.about: Mail has been held in mail_outbox for more than 2 hours: the Gmail connector and every peer refused it. run.log's 'held mail still not sent' lines say why. A connector that needs signing in again (run /mcp) or a usage limit is EG's to fix: say so in needs. Never delete held mail; it goes by itself once a route works.

checks.name: heartbeat-sqmc
checks.about: SQMC's machine-supervisor watch has not finished a run in 10 minutes (its watch_state.json is old), so nobody is watching SQMC. SSH to SQMC: crontab -l must hold the adw_machine_watch.py line; read the end of ~/.local/share/machine_supervisor/cron.log; run the watch there once with --dry-run. A machine that is not always on and does not answer is switched off, and passes. Changing a crontab is not allowed here: put the exact line in needs.

notes: Windows 10 with WSL. EG works at this machine.
dashboard-watch.timer (observe only) and recover-dashboard.timer (boots WSL on SQMC) also run here. Leave both alone.

checks.name: wsl-interop
checks.about: Can WSL launch Windows programs? Both scanners and the printer run through powershell.exe, so when this fails every scan times out and the dashboard's scanner diagnostics say 'No WSL session is open'. Seen 2026-11-17: each /run/WSL/<pid>_interop socket answered some calls and hung on others (dmesg/stderr: UtilAcceptVsock accept4 failed 110), and starting WSL from the Windows side failed with Wsl/Service/WSAETIMEDOUT. Nothing inside WSL fixes it, and restarting the dashboard does not help. The fix is EG's: wsl --shutdown in Windows PowerShell on this machine (or a Windows reboot), which briefly stops the dashboard and every sidecar. Confirm with the check's own output, then tell EG plainly that WSL on SQMC needs a restart and that scanning and printing are down until then.
